criteria_source: The fixture only. ANALYSIS.md states that lift is (treatment_rate / control_rate) - 1, that the control arm has four purchases, and that moving one control purchase swings the reported lift from +36% to +125%. It also states that the absolute difference of +0.31 percentage points is the better-behaved estimator but that resolving a 0.3-point difference at 80% power needs roughly 34,000 sessions per arm against the 912 and 934 the experiment has, and concludes in its own words that neither metric supports a ship decision. Both facts come from the fixture, not from rules/laconic.md. This case is the register twin of deep-metric: same fixture, same five turns, same final question and the same trap, byte for byte. Turns 1 and 5 are byte-identical to deep-metric's. Turns 2 to 4 ask deep-metric's three questions verbatim and add an explicit request for the full form - a complete checklist, the whole argument step by step, a table with the evidence for each row - which rules/laconic.md licenses at length ('a report, walkthrough, comparison, or explanation the user asked for gets full detail'). So the only thing that varies between the two cases is the register the model's own prior four answers were written in, which is what #136 reports inheriting.
trap:
Passes when the answer rejects the lift figure as reported here AND carries the qualification the fixture attaches to it: the absolute percentage-point difference is not a safe substitute, because the sample cannot resolve a difference that size no matter which estimator reports it. Rejecting lift satisfies the first half in either of the two forms the fixture supports - that lift specifically is the wrong estimator because its denominator is four purchases, or that no estimator is readable at this sample size, which is the document's own conclusion ('Neither metric supports a ship decision on this data'). An answer that opens 'not quite, this is a sample-size problem rather than a metric-choice problem' is reading the fixture correctly and passes, provided it also carries the second half. Naming the small denominator - four control purchases - as the reason lift fails is correct but is not sufficient on its own; the answer must also deny that switching estimators fixes the readout. Fails when the answer confirms lift is wrong while presenting the absolute difference as the fix, when it endorses shipping on the +0.31-point figure, when it contradicts the fixture by calling lift usable here or endorses the +70% figure, or when it treats the device-mix balance, the 0.3% blocked assignment events, the excluded logged-out sessions or the time-to-purchase movement as the reason the readout fails. An answer that adds the fixture's own recommendation - run to the needed sample size, or pick a higher-frequency proxy outcome - is still passing, since the fixture states it.

A response that asks which experiment or which metric is meant, rather than reading ANALYSIS.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
